meta.title: Taping technique — Palsya
meta.description: The taping techniques across the programme, with yours highlighted.

taping.pageSub: Three techniques across the programme. Yours is highlighted — the others are here so you can see where this goes.
taping.patchTestBody: A 3 cm piece on your inner forearm for 24 hours. And never tape across the eyelid unless a clinician has shown you a specific technique for it.

safety.s1: Skin must be clean, dry, and free of oils or creams. Tape will not hold otherwise.
safety.s2: Round the corners of every strip — square corners lift and catch on clothing.
safety.s3: Rub the tape for 10 seconds after applying. The adhesive is heat-activated.
safety.s4: Remove tape slowly, in the direction of hair growth, ideally in the shower.
safety.s5: Remove immediately and stop if you get itching, burning, a rash, or blistering.
safety.s6: Never tape across the eyelid or inside the eye socket.
safety.s7: Do not tape over broken, sunburnt, or infected skin.
safety.s8: Take a rest day from tape at least once a week to let the skin recover.

exercises.title: Facial exercises
exercises.sub: The {n} exercises in your programme at Stage {stage}, plus the ones that come later.
exercises.thirdEffortTitle: Roughly a third of your maximum effort.
exercises.thirdEffortBody: If you are gritting your teeth or holding your breath, you are far past it. This feels like not really trying, and it is the correct dose.
exercises.noneNow: No exercises at this stage — the programme is deliberately quiet right now.
exercises.notYet: Not yet. Doing these ahead of your stage is one of the ways people slow themselves down.

meta.title: Daily routine — Palsya
meta.description: Eye care, eating, massage, sleep and speech — the part of recovery that is not exercises.

routine.title: Daily routine
routine.sub: The part that is not exercises, and is roughly three quarters of what makes recovery go well.
routine.eyeCareTitle: If your eye does not close fully, eye care outranks every exercise in your programme.
routine.eyeCareBody: Corneal damage from exposure is the one complication of facial paralysis that can cause lasting harm, and it is largely preventable. Pain, redness, or changed vision means a doctor today.
